'''Anatoli Petrovich Bugorski''' ({{langx|ru|Анатолий Петрович Бугорский|link=no}}; born 25 June 1942) is a Russian retired particle physicist. He is known for having survived a [[radiation accident]] in 1978, when a high-energy proton beam from a [[particle accelerator]] passed through his head.<ref name="wired_future_ruins" /><ref name="discover_magazine">{{Cite web |title=If You Stuck Your Head in a Particle Accelerator ...|url=https://www.discovermagazine.com/health/if-you-stuck-your-head-in-a-particle-accelerator|access-date=18 August 2021|website=Discover Magazine|language=en|archive-date=18 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210818103323/https://www.discovermagazine.com/health/if-you-stuck-your-head-in-a-particle-accelerator|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Accident ==
As a researcher at the [[Institute for High Energy Physics]] in [[Protvino]], Russian SFSR<!-- DO NOT LINK, see [[MOS:GEOLINK]] for further guidance -->, Bugorski worked with the largest [[particle accelerator]] in the [[Soviet Union]], the [[U-70 (synchrotron)|U-70 synchrotron]].<ref name="gd-info_km_ru_personal">{{cite news |url=http://www.eco-pravda.ru/page.php?al=bugorsky_casus |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425115650/http://www.eco-pravda.ru/page.php?al=bugorsky_casus |script-title=ru:Персональный Чернобыль Анатолия Бугорского |language=Russian |newspaper=[[Izvestiya]] |via=Экологическая правда |date=23 January 1998 |accessdate=28 October 2011 |archive-date=25 April 2012 |trans-title=Anatoli Bugorski's Personal Chernobyl}}</ref> On 3 June 1978, he was checking a malfunctioning piece of equipment when the safety mechanisms failed. Bugorski was leaning over the equipment when he stuck his head in the path of the {{convert|76|GeV|abbr=on}} [[proton beam]]. He reportedly saw a flash "brighter than a thousand suns" but did not feel any pain.<ref name="wired_future_ruins">{{cite magazine |first1=Masha |last1=Gessen |author-link=Masha Gessen |date=1 December 1997 |title=The Future Ruins of the Nuclear Age |url=https://www.wired.com/1997/12/science-2/ |magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |access-date=28 March 2025 |archive-date=8 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241108095342/https://www.wired.com/1997/12/science-2/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The beam passed through the back of his head, the [[Occipital lobe|occipital]] and [[temporal lobe]]s of his brain, the left [[middle ear]], and out through the left-hand side of his nose. The exposed parts of his head received a local dose of 200,000 to 300,000 [[Roentgen (unit)|roentgens]] (2,000 to 3,000 [[Sievert|sieverts]]).<ref name="gd-info_km_ru_personal" /> Bugorski understood the severity of what had happened, but continued working on the malfunctioning equipment, and initially opted not to tell anyone what had happened.<ref name="gd-info_km_ru_personal" />

== Aftermath ==
Doctors expected him to die, but he survived with severe, non-fatal injuries. The left half of Bugorski's face swelled up beyond recognition and, over the next several days, the skin started to peel, revealing the path that the proton beam had burned through parts of his face, his bone, and the brain tissue underneath.<ref name="gizmodo">{{cite web |url=https://gizmodo.com/what-happens-when-you-stick-your-head-into-a-particle-a-1171981874 |title=What Happens When You Stick Your Head Into a Particle Accelerator |date=20 August 2013 |website=Gizmodo |access-date=3 December 2017 |archive-date=20 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130820182059/https://gizmodo.com/what-happens-when-you-stick-your-head-into-a-particle-a-1171981874 |url-status=live }}</ref> As it was believed that he had received far in excess of a fatal dose of radiation, Bugorski was taken to a clinic in Moscow where the doctors could observe his expected demise. However, Bugorski survived, completed his PhD, and continued working as a particle physicist.<ref>{{cite web |title=Catalog Card: Bugorski, Anatoli Petrovich, 'Optimization and control of neutrino streams (anti-neutrinos) in neutrino experiments at IHEP: Abstract of a dissertation for the degree of candidate of physical and mathematical sciences' |url=http://nlr.ru/e-case3/sc2.php/web_gak/lc/11901/153#pict |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622132756/http://www.nlr.ru/e-case3/sc2.php/web_gak/lc/11901/153 |archive-date=22 June 2015 |access-date=21 August 2020 |page=153 |series=Разделитель: Буглай Борис Мартынович Канд. техн. наук [Separator: Buglai Boris Martynovich Cand. tech. sciences] |department=Генеральный алфавитный каталог книг на русском языке (1725 - 1998) [General Alphabetical Catalog of Russian-Language Books (1725–1998)] |publisher=[[National Library of Russia]] |location=Saint Petersburg, Russia |language=ru}}</ref> There was virtually no damage to his intellectual capacity, but the fatigue of mental work increased markedly.<ref name="gd-info_km_ru_personal" /> Bugorski completely [[Hearing loss|lost hearing]] in the left ear, replaced by a form of [[tinnitus]].<ref name="gd-info_km_ru_personal"/><ref name="discover_magazine"/> The left half of his face became [[Facial paralysis|paralysed]] due to the destruction of [[Facial nerve paralysis|nerves]].<ref name="wired_future_ruins" /> He was able to function well, except for occasional [[complex partial seizure]]s and rare [[tonic-clonic seizure]]s. The paralysed side of his face does not have wrinkles.<ref name="wired_future_ruins"/>

Bugorski continued to work as a physicist at the [[Institute for High Energy Physics]], eventually becoming the experiment coordinator for the same particle accelerator by which he was injured.<ref name="gd-info_km_ru_personal" />

Because of the Soviet Union's policy of maintaining secrecy on [[nuclear power]]-related issues, Bugorski did not speak publicly about the accident for over a decade. He continued going to the Moscow radiation clinic twice a year for examinations and to meet with other nuclear accident victims. He was described as "a [[poster boy]] for Soviet and Russian radiation medicine".<ref name="wired_future_ruins" />

In 1996, Bugorski applied unsuccessfully for disability status to receive free [[epilepsy]] medication.<ref name="wired_future_ruins"/> Bugorski showed interest in making himself available for study to Western researchers but could not afford to leave [[Protvino]].<ref name="wired_future_ruins" /><ref name="gizmodo" />

==Personal life==
Bugorski is married to Vera Nikolaevna, and they have a son.<ref name="gd-info_km_ru_personal" />
